sentences.text:
This appeal by the claimant under Section 173(1) of the Indian Motor Vehicles Act is filed against the judgment and award dated 09.04.2018, passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT-IV at Davangere in MVC No.341/2016.
2.

The claimant, while driving a milk van, was involved in an accident where the offending vehicle,
approaching from the opposite direction, collided with the milk van, causing the claimant to sustain injuries.

The tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.3,40,700/- with interest at the rate of 8%
per annum but attributed 50% contributory negligence to the claimant.
Consequently, respondent No.3, the insurance company, was held liable to pay only 50% of the awarded compensation.
3. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
The police, after their investigation, submitted a charge sheet against both the claimant and the driver of the offending vehicle, which was produced as Exhibit P3.

The spot mahazar, marked as Exhibit P4, indicated that the accident occurred on the left side of the road where the claimant was A N Mahendra vs Gangadhara A N on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105271364/
2 driving his milk van.

sentences.text: This spot mahazar was not disputed by the respondent/insurance company.

A review of Exhibit P4 showed that the driver of the offending vehicle was on the extreme right side of the road when the collision occurred, thereby hitting the milk van, which was proceeding on the correct side of the road.

Therefore, it is concluded that the Tribunal erred in attributing 50%
contributory negligence to the claimant.
5. The accident occurred in 2015.
In the absence of proof of income, the notional income of the claimant is assessed at Rs.9,000/- per month, as opposed to the Rs.8,000/- per month assessed by the tribunal.

The doctor, who was examined as PW.2, assessed the claimant's functional disability at 30% due to fractures sustained in the upper third of both the right leg bones, including the tibia and condyle, along with popliteal artery contusion.
The claimant underwent surgery and was discharged on 16.07.2015, having been an inpatient for nearly ten days.
The claimant, being a driver of a transport vehicle by profession, is assessed to have a permanent functional disability of 15%, as opposed to the 10% assessed by the tribunal.

Consequently, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is reassessed as follows:
 Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-
 Food, Nourishment and
Attendant
charges Rs.20,000/-

Loss of income during later  Period Rs.27,000/-
 Medical expenses Rs.78,500/-
 Loss of Amenities Rs.25,000/-
 Loss of Income due to  Disability Rs.2,75,400/-

Future medical expenses Rs.20,000/-
5.
The claimant in all is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,95,900/- as against Rs,3,40,700/-.
The enhanced compensation amount of Rs.1,70,359/- shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till actual realization.
The respondent No.3-Insurance Company is fastened with the entire liability to pay the compensation to the claimant.
To this extent the impugned award stands modified.
